\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Threshold Functions --- Sparse Sampling}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.SparseSampling
\section{Overview}
Finite independent sampling and uniform concentration give a signed-character approximation to any nonzero real cube function, controlled by its spectral one-norm.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[One-sided concentration of bounded independent samples]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sample_tail}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $s>0$ be an integer and $Y_1,\ldots,Y_s$ be independent real functions on a probability space $(\Omega,\mu)$, each measurable up to a null set and valued in $[-1,1]$ almost surely, with common mean $\mathbb E Y_i=m$. Write $\Pr(A)=\mu^*(A)$ for outer probability. For every real $\varepsilon\ge0$, $\Pr[s\varepsilon\le\sum_iY_i-sm]\le\exp(-s\varepsilon^2/2)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Two-sided concentration of bounded independent samples]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sample_abs_tail}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sample_tail}
\difficulty{4}
Let $s>0$ be an integer and $Y_1,\ldots,Y_s$ be independent real functions on a probability space $(\Omega,\mu)$, each measurable up to a null set and valued in $[-1,1]$ almost surely, with common mean $\mathbb E Y_i=m$. Write $\Pr(A)=\mu^*(A)$ for outer probability. For every real $\varepsilon\ge0$, $\Pr[s\varepsilon\le|\sum_iY_i-sm|]\le2\exp(-s\varepsilon^2/2)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A strict numerical bound for positive dimension]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sparse_numeric}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every positive integer $n$, $2^{n+1}e^{-2n}<1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sample size implies an exponent bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sparse_param}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,s\ge0$ be integers and $L,\delta>0$ be real numbers. If $4nL^2/\delta^2\le s$, then $2n\le s(\delta/L)^2/2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A uniform concentration sum is below one]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sparse_union_numeric}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sparse_numeric, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sparse_param}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n>0$ and $s\ge0$ be integers and $L,\delta>0$ be real numbers with $4nL^2/\delta^2\le s$. Then $2^n\bigl(2\exp(-s(\delta/L)^2/2)\bigr)<1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A point outside a finite family of small events]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.exists_good_of_union_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $J$ be a finite index set, and let $(A_j)_{j\in J}$ be arbitrary subsets of $\Omega$. If a real number $B$ satisfies $\mu^*(A_j)\le B$ for every $j$ and $|J|B<1$, then some $\omega\in\Omega$ belongs to none of the $A_j$, where $\mu^*$ denotes the outer measure of $\mu$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A distribution with the normalized Fourier mean]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sparse_sample_pmf_mean}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.abs_mul_thresholdSign, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.spectralOneNorm, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.thresholdSign, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.walsh_expansion}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\ge0$ and give $\{0,1\}^n$ uniform probability; write $\mathbb E$ for expectation. Put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ and real cube functions $h$. Write $\operatorname{sgn}_+(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$. For a real cube function $f$ with $L=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}|\widehat f(S)|>0$, there exists a probability distribution $\pi$ on the subsets of $[n]$ such that $\mathbb E_{S\sim\pi}[\operatorname{sgn}_+(\widehat f(S))\chi_S(x)]=f(x)/L$ for every cube point $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A nonzero cube function has positive spectral one-norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.spectralOneNorm_pos}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.spectralOneNorm, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.spectralOneNorm_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.walsh_expansion}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\ge0$ and give $\{0,1\}^n$ uniform probability; write $\mathbb E$ for expectation. Put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ and real cube functions $h$. If a real cube function $f$ is not identically zero, then its spectral one-norm $\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}|\widehat f(S)|$ is strictly positive.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform approximation by signed Fourier samples]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sparse_signed_sample}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.exists_good_of_union_bound, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sample_abs_tail, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sparse_sample_pmf_mean, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sparse_union_numeric, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.spectralOneNorm, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.spectralOneNorm_pos, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.thresholdSign, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.chiS_sq_eq_one, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n\ge0$ and give $\{0,1\}^n$ uniform probability; write $\mathbb E$ for expectation. Put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ and real cube functions $h$. Write $\operatorname{sgn}_+(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$. Let $n>0$, let $f$ be a real cube function not identically zero, put $L=\sum_S|\widehat f(S)|$, and let $\delta>0$ and an integer $s\ge0$ satisfy $4nL^2/\delta^2\le s$. There exists a sequence of subsets $T_1,\ldots,T_s\subseteq[n]$, with repetitions allowed, such that $|f(x)-(L/s)\sum_{j=1}^s\operatorname{sgn}_+(\widehat f(T_j))\chi_{T_j}(x)|<\delta$ for every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$.
\end{theorem}
